comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, one customer accounted for approximately 24% and another for 16% of total consolidated accounts receivable, though the Company does not believe these balances represent significant credit risk due to past collection experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose that a single customer accounts for a significant percentage of their consolidated accounts receivable balance, exceeding 15% in both cases. However, the specific metrics and credit risk assessments differ. AVGO discloses that one customer accounted for 18% of net accounts receivable as of November 3, 2024, and notes that this same customer represented 28% of net revenue in fiscal year 2024. AMD discloses that one customer accounted for approximately 24% of total consolidated accounts receivable as of December 28, 2024, but explicitly states it does not believe this balance represents significant credit risk, whereas AVGO does not provide a similar credit risk disclaimer for its top customer.

sentences.text: One customer accounted for 18% and 21% of our net accounts receivable balance as of November 3, 2024 and October 29, 2023, respectively.
During fiscal years 2024, 2023 and 2022, one customer accounted for 28%, 21% and 20% of our net revenue, respectively.
One customer accounted for approximately 24% and another customer accounted for 16% of the total consolidated accounts receivable balance as of December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, respectively.
However, the Company does not believe the receivable balance from these customers represents a significant credit risk based on past collection experience and review of their current credit quality.
